items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I was trying to play a Thelonious Monk thing on the piano

ctx.x: Which there are an awful lot of books now, aren’t there?

Oh yeah, a lot of books man. There weren’t any books like that when I was coming up on how to — now there are a lot of books but that could serve you well if you know how to use them. But at some point you have to get away from the book. You have to take the knowledge in the book and turn it inside out. Like today, and I’ve always taught, about printed music. Printed music has the function of being able to play from the top of the music all the way down, no mistakes, understand everything about the rhythm, the…
like that. You couldn’t do that man. But even teaching in the jazz like I wound up doing, I didn’t go to school for that but my school was out there, doing it.
